clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work and then separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. These shifts pile up across the family in the months after the death, each touching on another, until your grandmother took a library job in May 1979 and began functioning again.

1984: your mother's fall in functioning when ordered to bed is the change that opens this span, and four shifts count among its events (your grandmother Hazel overfunctioning, your father's conflict with her, your brother Callum's stammer, and your anxiety at bedtime marked unknown date). However, the period you named covers these same years, so this hint's events fall within your period and are left out rather than drawn again.

1986–1997: your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis of Parkinson's disease in September 1986 opens this span. Fourteen shifts count: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioning, your father's anxiety rising, your grandmother's functioning falling and rising, conflict between your grandfather and father, your uncle Lyle's distance from your parents marked unknown date, your grandfather's chest pains, your grandmother's functioning falling again, your mother overfunctioning, your aunt Mavis toward your grandmother, your uncle Duncan's drinking rising, your aunt Pearl's anxiety rising, your grandmother's functioning falling once more, and your uncle Duncan's fights with your mother. The period ends when your grandmother moved into the Fairlie nursing home in June 1997 and your uncle Duncan cut his drinking back to weekends in October. This is a long climb over years with shifts marking each step and no quiet between them long enough to settle, so the family's reactions to her decline held over the decade.

1999–2000: your brother Callum's leaving home for a job in the mines in May 1999 opens this span. Six shifts count: your father and brother in conflict over his plans, your mother's anxiety rising, your father's functioning falling, your sister Ines's functioning falling, your mother toward your sister, and your sister's functioning rising again by August 2000. The period ends when your sister went back to school full days and passed her exams. These shifts are your sister's own trouble and the reactions between your parents and her; your father's and mother's shifts toward or around your sister sit beside the opening, and no one else's shifts show in these months.

2003: your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003 opens this span, which is your own period you named. This hint's events fall within the years you drew, so it is answered by your period and left out here.

2005-11-19 to 2005-11-23: your sister Ines's car accident on black ice is a real threat with several shifts dated within the same few days. Your mother sat up all night by the phone, your father could not keep food down, your brother came down overnight to her bedside, your sister shook at the thought of the ride home, and your mother was calm once your sister was home and up and about. All shifts fall within four days around the accident and hospital stay, with settling within days of the start; this is an acute episode around a real event, not a period.
